post.title: You Forgot Why You Walked In? Blame the Door #shorts
post.description: June walks into the kitchen and forgets why. Psychologists Gabriel Radvansky, Sabine Krawietz and Andrea Tamplin (2011, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology) found that walking through a doorway, in virtual and real rooms, made people slower and less accurate at remembering what they were carrying than walking the same distance inside one room. A doorway works like an event boundary: your brain files the old scene away. #psychology #shorts #memory
